question: Under Section 475.15, F.S., which types of business organizations acting as a real estate broker must register with the commission and renew the licenses/registrations of their members, officers, and directors each license period?
choice_a: Partnerships, limited liability partnerships, limited liability companies, and corporations that act as a broker
choice_b: Only corporations, never partnerships or limited liability companies
choice_c: Only sole proprietorships operating under a broker's individual name
choice_d: Only publicly traded real estate investment trusts
explanation: Section 475.15, F.S. requires every partnership, limited liability partnership, limited liability company, or corporation that acts as a broker to register with the commission and to renew the licenses or registrations of its members, officers, and directors for each license period.
source_note: Section 475.15, F.S. (Registration and licensing of general partners, members, officers, and directors of a firm)

question: In a Florida real estate brokerage organized as a limited partnership, which partners must be licensed brokers (or brokerage corporations registered under Chapter 475)?
choice_a: Only the general partners
choice_b: Every limited partner, regardless of role
choice_c: No partners at all; only the partnership entity itself needs a license
choice_d: Only whichever partner personally shows properties to the public
explanation: Section 475.15, F.S. specifically provides that if the partnership is a limited partnership, only the general partners must be licensed brokers or brokerage corporations registered under Part I of Chapter 475 -- limited partners, who by definition do not participate in management, are not subject to this licensing requirement.

question: A real estate brokerage corporation's registration automatically cancels for the period during which:
choice_a: The license or registration of at least one active broker member/officer of the corporation is not in force
choice_b: The corporation changes its business mailing address
choice_c: A single sales associate's individual license becomes inactive
choice_d: The corporation's annual revenue drops below a stated threshold
explanation: Under Section 475.15, F.S., if the license or registration of at least one active broker member is not in force, the registration of the corporation, LLC, LLP, or partnership is automatically canceled during that period -- reflecting the requirement that an entity brokerage always have at least one active licensed broker.

question: Section 475.15, F.S. directs the commission to adopt rules allowing a brokerage to register a broker on what basis if the sole broker of the brokerage dies or is unexpectedly unable to remain a broker?
choice_a: A temporary, emergency basis
choice_b: No basis; the brokerage must immediately dissolve
choice_c: A permanent basis with no further application ever required
choice_d: Only if a circuit court order authorizes continued operation
explanation: Section 475.15, F.S. requires the commission to adopt rules that allow a brokerage to register a broker on a temporary, emergency basis when the sole broker of a brokerage dies or is unexpectedly unable to remain a broker, preventing an otherwise-compliant brokerage from being forced to shut down immediately.

question: If a brokerage's sole active broker dies or resigns, F.A.C. 61J2-5.018 requires the brokerage to register a replacement broker within how many calendar days to avoid automatic cancellation of the brokerage's registration?
choice_a: 14 calendar days
choice_b: 90 calendar days
choice_c: 180 calendar days
choice_d: There is no deadline, as long as a broker is eventually found
explanation: F.A.C. 61J2-5.018 (Vacancies of Office) requires a brokerage whose sole active broker has died or resigned to register a replacement broker within 14 calendar days; failing to do so results in automatic cancellation of the brokerage's registration and inactivation of its associates' licenses.

question: A temporary broker registered to fill a vacancy left by a deceased or resigned sole active broker under F.A.C. 61J2-5.018 may serve for a maximum of:
choice_a: 60 days, by which point proof that a permanent broker is properly registered with the Secretary of State must be filed
choice_b: One full two-year license renewal cycle
choice_c: 5 business days
choice_d: An indefinite period, with no outer limit
explanation: Under F.A.C. 61J2-5.018, a temporary broker may serve a brokerage for up to 60 days without needing to comply with Secretary of State registration requirements; by the end of that 60-day window, the brokerage must file proof that a permanent broker has been properly registered.

question: F.A.C. 61J2-5.019 places a specific duty on every active corporate officer and director of a brokerage corporation to:
choice_a: See that the corporation and each of its officers hold current registration and licenses
choice_b: Personally supervise every sales associate's individual transactions
choice_c: Personally approve every advertisement the brokerage publishes
choice_d: Co-sign every listing agreement the brokerage enters into
explanation: F.A.C. 61J2-5.019 (Responsibility for Registration Status) makes it the duty of every active corporate officer and director to see that the corporation and each of its officers and directors are holders of current registration and licenses -- a distinct entity-level compliance duty separate from a broker's day-to-day supervision of sales associates' transactions.

question: Under F.A.C. 61J2-5.020, applications and papers submitted on behalf of a brokerage corporation must be:
choice_a: Signed in the name of the corporation by an active broker officer or director
choice_b: Signed by any employee designated by a majority vote of shareholders
choice_c: Notarized by the corporation's registered agent only, regardless of license status
choice_d: Submitted without any signature, since corporate filings are self-executing
explanation: F.A.C. 61J2-5.020 (Execution of Papers by Corporation) requires that all applications submitted on behalf of a brokerage corporation be signed in the name of the corporation by an active broker officer or director -- ensuring a licensed, accountable individual stands behind the corporation's filings.

question: Under F.A.C. 61J2-5.017, an inactive officer or director of a brokerage corporation:
choice_a: Is not individually required to file a renewal application; registration is maintained based on the corporation's representations
choice_b: Must personally appear before the commission every renewal cycle
choice_c: Automatically loses all corporate officer status the moment they go inactive
choice_d: Must complete active-broker post-licensing education despite remaining inactive
explanation: F.A.C. 61J2-5.017 (Registration of Inactive Officers and Directors) provides that individual renewal applications are not required of inactive officers and directors of a corporation; their registration is instead maintained on the basis of the representations contained in the corporation's own application or renewal.
source_note: F.A.C. 61J2-5.017 (Registration of Inactive Officers and Directors)

question: Section 475.161, F.S. allows a broker associate or sales associate to be licensed as a professional corporation, limited liability company, or professional limited liability company for their own individual practice, but this provision does NOT allow such an associate to:
choice_a: Register as a general partner, member, manager, officer, or director of the brokerage firm itself under Section 475.15
choice_b: Ever earn commission income through the brokerage
choice_c: Work for more than one broker over the course of a career
choice_d: Include their own name in personal marketing materials
explanation: While Section 475.161, F.S. lets a broker associate or sales associate be licensed individually or through a professional corporation/LLC/PLLC (with Department of State authorization) for personal practice, it does not extend to allowing that associate to hold a brokerage-firm management or ownership role -- general partner, member, manager, officer, or director positions under Section 475.15 remain reserved for licensed brokers.

question: Section 475.22, F.S. requires that each active broker maintain an office consisting of:
choice_a: At least one enclosed room in a building of stationary construction
choice_b: A minimum of 500 square feet of retail street frontage
choice_c: A home office only, since commercial locations are prohibited
choice_d: No physical office at all, provided the broker operates exclusively online
explanation: Section 475.22(1), F.S. requires every active broker to maintain an office consisting of at least one enclosed room in a building of stationary construction -- a purely virtual or mobile-only 'office' does not satisfy this statutory requirement.

question: Under Section 475.22, F.S., a sign posted at the entrance of a broker's principal office (and any branch office) must, at minimum, include:
choice_a: The broker's name (and trade name, if any) along with the words 'licensed real estate broker' or 'lic. real estate broker'
choice_b: The broker's personal cell phone number only
choice_c: A list of every sales associate currently registered with the brokerage
choice_d: The brokerage's most recent annual sales volume figures
explanation: Section 475.22(1), F.S. requires an office entrance sign showing, at minimum, the broker's name (and trade name, if one is used) together with the words 'licensed real estate broker' or the abbreviation 'lic. real estate broker' -- identifying the office to the public as a licensed brokerage location.

question: A broker whose registered office is located outside Florida must, under Section 475.22, F.S.:
choice_a: Agree in writing to cooperate with DBPR investigations, including providing requested documents and appearing for interviews
choice_b: Maintain a second, in-state office staffed at all times
choice_c: Waive all Florida license law obligations in exchange for nonresident status
choice_d: Appoint a Florida-licensed broker as a silent co-owner of the brokerage
explanation: Section 475.22(2), F.S. requires a broker whose registered office is outside Florida to agree in writing to cooperate with department investigations, including promptly furnishing requested documents and appearing for interviews; failing to comply with a certified-mail request is itself a license law violation subject to discipline under Section 475.25, F.S.

question: Under F.A.C. 61J2-10.023, each additional office a brokerage operates beyond its principal office must be:
choice_a: Separately registered as a branch office with DBPR, along with payment of the applicable branch office fee
choice_b: Left unregistered, as long as the same broker supervises it
choice_c: Registered only once it generates more than half the brokerage's annual revenue
choice_d: Registered with the local county clerk in place of DBPR
explanation: F.A.C. 61J2-10.023 requires every additional office beyond a brokerage's principal office to be separately registered as a branch office with DBPR, with payment of the applicable fee -- operating an unregistered additional office is a licensure compliance failure regardless of who supervises it.

question: F.A.C. 61J2-10.023 exempts which type of location from branch office registration?
choice_a: A temporary subdivision sales shelter at which transactions are not actually closed on-site
choice_b: Any location used by the brokerage more than three days per week
choice_c: Any office with fewer than five sales associates assigned to it
choice_d: The brokerage's own principal office
explanation: Under F.A.C. 61J2-10.023, branch office status turns on the permanence, use, and character of activities customarily conducted at a location; a temporary sales shelter on a subdivision where transactions are not actually closed is exempt from separate branch office registration, unlike a genuine additional place of business.

question: If a brokerage closes a registered branch office and later wants to open a new office at a different location, F.A.C. 61J2-10.023 requires:
choice_a: A separate new branch office registration and fee, since a closed branch's registration cannot simply transfer to the new location
choice_b: Nothing further, since the original branch registration automatically follows the brokerage
choice_c: Written approval from every sales associate previously assigned to the closed branch
choice_d: A formal commission hearing before the new office may open
explanation: F.A.C. 61J2-10.023 treats a closed branch office registration as terminated rather than transferable; opening a new office at a different location requires its own separate branch office registration and fee payment.

question: Under F.A.C. 61J2-10.038, a licensee who changes their current mailing address or e-mail address must notify DBPR within:
choice_a: 10 days of the change
choice_b: 60 days of the change
choice_c: One full license renewal cycle
choice_d: There is no notification requirement as long as mail is eventually forwarded
explanation: F.A.C. 61J2-10.038 requires a licensee to notify the department of any change in current mailing address or e-mail address within 10 days of the change; a first violation typically draws a citation, while subsequent violations can trigger formal disciplinary proceedings.

question: Under F.A.C. 61J2-10.026, a sales team or group operating within a brokerage must:
choice_a: Operate under the supervision of the same broker
choice_b: Register as its own separate brokerage entity apart from the sponsoring broker
choice_c: Maintain its own independent escrow account apart from the brokerage's escrow account
choice_d: Obtain a distinct commission license separate from its individual members' licenses
explanation: F.A.C. 61J2-10.026 (Team or Group Advertising) requires that a sales team or group operate under the supervision of the same broker; a team is not a separate licensed entity and does not maintain its own escrow account or license independent of the brokerage.

question: Under F.A.C. 61J2-10.026, a sales team's chosen name generally may NOT include words that:
choice_a: Imply the team is a separate brokerage entity, such as 'agency,' 'brokerage,' 'corp,' or 'LLC'
choice_b: Include any individual team member's first name
choice_c: Exceed 10 characters in total length
choice_d: Reference the geographic area the team serves
explanation: F.A.C. 61J2-10.026 prohibits a sales team's name from including words that suggest the team is a separate brokerage entity -- such as 'agency,' 'brokerage,' 'company,' 'corporation,' or 'LLC' -- since the team operates under, and only under, the sponsoring broker's own brokerage.

question: Under F.A.C. 61J2-10.026, a brokerage operating sales teams must additionally:
choice_a: Designate one team member responsible for the team's advertising compliance and maintain a current written roster of team members
choice_b: Pay each team member a fixed salary independent of any commission earned
choice_c: Limit every team to no more than two members
choice_d: File a separate trust account statement for each individual team
explanation: F.A.C. 61J2-10.026 requires that one licensee within each team be designated as responsible for the team's advertising compliance, and requires the broker to maintain a current written record of team membership, updated regularly -- administrative safeguards tied to the broker's overall supervisory responsibility for team-branded marketing.

question: Which statutory provision authorizes FREC to discipline a broker specifically for failing to direct, control, or manage a broker associate or sales associate registered under that broker?
choice_a: Section 475.25(1)(u), F.S.
choice_b: Section 475.161, F.S.
choice_c: Section 475.42(1)(a), F.S.
choice_d: Section 475.15, F.S.
explanation: Section 475.25(1)(u), F.S. specifically authorizes FREC discipline against a broker who has failed to direct, control, or manage a broker associate or sales associate employed by or registered under that broker -- distinct from Section 475.42's unlicensed-activity provisions and Sections 475.15/475.161's entity-registration and associate-licensing rules.
